test_title: PYST 31: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I - Mathematics (Held On: 18 Jun, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: maths
question: A boat takes 18 minutes to go 59.4 km upstream. The ratio of the speed of the boat in still water to that of the stream is 3 : 2. How much total time (in hours) will the boat take to go 29.3 km upstream and 51.5 km downstream?
solution:
**Given:**

Time to go upstream = 18 minutes = 18/60 hours = 0.3 hours

Distance covered upstream = 59.4 km

Ratio of speed of the boat in still water to that of the stream = 3 : 2

Distance to cover upstream = 29.3 km

Distance to cover downstream = 51.5 km

**Formula used:**

Speed = Distance / Time

Let the speed of the boat in still water = 3x, and the speed of the stream = 2x.

Upstream speed = (Speed of boat in still water - Speed of stream) = (3x - 2x) = x

Downstream speed = (Speed of boat in still water + Speed of stream) = (3x + 2x) = 5x

Total time = (Time taken upstream) + (Time taken downstream)

**Calculations:**

Given, Time to go upstream = 0.3 hours and Distance covered upstream = 59.4 km

⇒ Upstream speed = Distance / Time

⇒ x = 59.4 / 0.3

⇒ x = 198 km/h

Speed of the boat in still water = 3x = 3 × 198 = 594 km/h

Speed of the stream = 2x = 2 × 198 = 396 km/h

Upstream speed = x = 198 km/h

Downstream speed = 5x = 5 × 198 = 990 km/h

Time to go 29.3 km upstream:

⇒ Time = Distance / Speed

⇒ Time = 29.3 / 198

⇒ Time = 0.148 hours

Time to go 51.5 km downstream:

⇒ Time = Distance / Speed

⇒ Time = 51.5 / 990

⇒ Time = 0.052 hours

Total time = Time taken upstream + Time taken downstream

⇒ Total time = 0.148 + 0.052

⇒ Total time = 0.2 hours

**∴ The correct answer is option (1).**
